01 · The lists

Pick your level,
start reading

Five word lists that follow the JLPT levels: each word in kanji or kana with its reading and an English meaning. The JLPT has published no official lists since 2010, so these follow the widely used sets built from the earlier syllabus and later exams. Pick a level, read the list, then let the widget carry it onto your Lock Screen.

03 · Questions

Asked and
answered

Which JLPT levels do these lists cover?

All five JLPT levels, N5 through N1, each as its own list and its own pack in the app. N5 is free in the app; every other level opens with a free preview and another word unlocks daily.

Where do the word lists come from?

Word lists: the widely used JLPT N5 to N1 sets after Jonathan Waller's tanos.co.uk lists (the JLPT publishes no official lists). Definitions adapted from JMdict by the EDRDG, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Example sentences are original Lock&Learn content.

Is Lock&Learn Japanese free?

Yes. The app is free on iOS: JLPT N5 is free, every other pack opens with a free preview, and another word unlocks daily. Lock&Learn+ is an optional upgrade that opens every pack at once, offered as a yearly plan or a one-time lifetime purchase.
